strengths: Mathematically rigorous development with proper proofs for geodesic PCA in Wasserstein spaces
Comprehensive treatment of both Gaussian and general probability measure cases
Clear visualizations demonstrating that discovered components capture meaningful modes of variation
Addresses a legitimate mathematical problem in statistical manifold learning
weaknesses: Incremental novelty: primarily extends existing geodesic PCA theory to Wasserstein spaces without fundamental methodological advances
No convergence guarantees for the proposed block alternating optimization algorithm, which is explicitly acknowledged by authors (page 22)
Weak experimental validation: limited baselines (mainly TPCA), only qualitative comparisons, no quantitative metrics demonstrating superiority over alternatives

Limited practical advantages demonstrated: method achieves comparable results to TPCA on Gaussian case with additional complexity; for general measures, unclear when this expensive approach would be preferred
Poor scalability and applicability: Wasserstein computations are expensive in high dimensions; all experiments are low-dimensional; no computational complexity analysis provided
Fundamental technical gaps: geodesic computation only defined on restricted time intervals; ad-hoc MLP parametrization; no ablation studies for extensive hyperparameter tuning
Insufficient scope for top-tier AI conference: primarily a differential geometry/statistics paper lacking clear machine learning innovations, algorithmic contributions, or real-world applications
Missing reproducibility information: no code availability mentioned, implementation details sparse, no timing or computational comparisons
Inadequate motivation: paper doesn't clearly explain when practitioners should use this method or why Wasserstein geometry is necessary versus simpler alternatives

strengths: Novel theoretical framework leveraging Otto's fiber bundle geometry to parametrize geodesics in Wasserstein space for PCA - mathematically elegant and original contribution
Comprehensive mathematical rigor with extensive proofs and self-contained background on Wasserstein geometry and differential geometry foundations
Well-motivated problem articulating clear limitations of existing approaches (TPCA, standard PCA) in capturing intrinsic structure of probability distributions
Dual-approach methodology providing both exact solutions for Gaussian distributions and a practical neural network-based algorithm for general a.c. measures
Diverse experimental validation across multiple domains (synthetic distributions, point clouds, landscape images, MNIST) demonstrating versatility
Clear and effective visualizations of geodesic principal components and their interpretations
weaknesses: Experiments lack quantitative evaluation metrics - most assessments are qualitative/visual with no objective comparison of geodesic quality or downstream task performance
Insufficient empirical validation of practical superiority over existing methods - limited baseline comparisons (TPCA only) and no comparison with alternative methods for general a.c. measures

Significant convergence guarantee issue acknowledged but inadequately addressed: block alternating algorithm convergence cannot be ensured due to non-uniqueness of minimizers, relegated to appendix with minimal main-text discussion
Missing computational complexity analysis - no discussion of computational costs, scalability, or training time comparison with alternatives despite expensive neural network training
Unclear practical necessity and applicability - paper does not articulate when practitioners should use GPCAGEN over simpler methods, and added complexity is not justified by experimental results

Algorithm design choices under-justified: use of MLPs to parametrize non-convex manifolds without verification, hyperparameter selection (λ₁=λ₂=1.0) lacks sensitivity analysis, and claimed 'exact recovery' of synthetic geodesics shows visible discrepancies
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned, critical implementation details relegated to appendices, computational requirements not fully specified
Restrictive assumptions limit applicability: exact solution requires centered non-degenerate Gaussian distributions; unclear sample complexity requirements for reliable geodesic estimation

strengths: Rigorous mathematical foundation grounded in differential geometry and optimal transport theory, with sound development of GPCA on Wasserstein spaces
Legitimate theoretical contributions establishing existence of minimizers for GPCA problems with orthogonality constraints (Propositions 12-13)
Clear algorithmic descriptions for both Gaussian and general a.c. measure cases with implementation details in appendices
Diverse experimental coverage including synthetic data, 3D point clouds, images, and weather datasets with reasonable visualizations
Reproducibility effort with code availability, documented hyperparameters, and comprehensive appendices
weaknesses: Weak experimental validation: primarily qualitative/visual results without quantitative metrics, reconstruction error analysis, or downstream task evaluation
Inappropriate baseline comparisons: TPCA acknowledged as operating on discrete approximations; missing comparisons with other Wasserstein-space PCA methods

Convergence not guaranteed: authors explicitly acknowledge non-convexity prevents convergence guarantees; block-alternating optimization employed without theoretical justification for this non-convex setting
Neural network approximation unvalidated: approximation error propagation from MLP implementations not analyzed; architecture choices (4-layer, 128 units) unjustified
Limited practical motivation: unclear when GPCA is preferable to simpler alternatives; multiple hyperparameters (λ_I, λ_O, λ_τ) require tuning with insufficient sensitivity analysis
Incremental novelty: primarily adapts existing GPCA and Wasserstein geometry concepts using standard neural network parameterization without novel technical innovations
Scalability and computational cost not addressed: no analysis of runtime or scaling properties compared to baselines; only tested on relatively small numbers of distributions

Design choice justification lacking: orthogonality definition appears somewhat arbitrary; minimizing reconstruction cost vs maximizing variance not motivated; applicability of real-world preprocessing (images/weather to distributions) questionable
Incomplete ablation studies: limited sensitivity analysis on key design choices; hyperparameter selection guidance insufficient for practitioners
Convergence not empirically verified: despite non-guaranteed convergence, no empirical analysis showing algorithm reliably finds good solutions in practice

strengths: Addresses an important and under-explored problem: geodesic PCA on probability measures in Wasserstein space with clear relevance to machine learning applications
Strong theoretical foundation with rigorous proofs connecting classical PCA, tangent PCA, and geodesic PCA on Riemannian manifolds; 16 well-established propositions
Dual algorithmic approach: exact solutions for Gaussian distributions with theoretical guarantees plus practical GPCAGen neural network method for general absolutely continuous measures
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple domains (synthetic Gaussians, 3D point clouds, images, weather data) with meaningful comparisons to baselines (TPCA, latent-space PCA)
Clear algorithmic contributions: Algorithm 1 (GPCAGen) is precisely specified and implementable; effective use of visualization (Figures 3-4, 6-7) to illustrate geodesic components
Elegant mathematical framework leveraging Otto's parametrization and Riemannian geometry; comprehensive appendices with detailed proofs enhance technical depth
Code availability commitment improves reproducibility; generally clear writing with good notation and organization
weaknesses: Gaussian case builds substantially on existing work (Huckemann & Ziezold 2006, Bigot et al. 2017); Proposition 5 for univariate case is a special case with limited new insights; novelty here is somewhat incremental

Significant theoretical gaps for general case: no convergence guarantees for the alternating algorithm (acknowledged in Section D.2 as unachievable due to non-convexity), no approximation error bounds for neural network parametrization, Proposition 5 explicitly open in higher dimensions

GPCAGen lacks theoretical justification for why MLPs should capture meaningful geodesic parametrizations; relationship between optimization objective (Eq. 15) and actual geodesic discovery for general measures not rigorously established

Incomplete convergence and scalability analysis: high-dimensional Hessian computation acknowledged as problematic (Section E.2.3) with proposed LOBPCG solution unevaluated; no computational complexity analysis or runtime comparisons; scalability with n and d not addressed

Experimental limitations: only TPCA and latent-space PCA compared (limited baselines); synthetic experiments with only 50 Gaussian matrices; weather and landscape experiments purely qualitative without metrics; outlier detection preliminary with arbitrary thresholds; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals

Numerous hyperparameters with limited selection guidance; grid search results show poor performance at λ_O=100 without explanation; sample complexity for distribution sampling not discussed; sensitivity analysis mostly in appendix with limited insight

Presentation: novel contributions vs. incremental improvements not clearly delineated; critical implementation details scattered across appendices; distinction between Gaussian-specific methods and GPCAGen approach poorly motivated; lacking practical guidance on when to use which method
Code URLs redacted in manuscript ('available at ___'); implementation details not fully reproducible; library versions unspecified; reproducibility could be stronger
